form_basis: "you shall receive no gifts" (23:8)
note: Bribe-taking and unjust acquittal are moral wrongs; addressed to those judging, so Civil second. 'Keep far away' is an avoidance duty, not a separate requirement.

form_basis: "you shall sow your land" (23:10)
note: 'You shall sow' sets the six working years beside the seventh-year release: an allowance, not a duty (as with six days' labour). Positive is the alternative reading.

form_basis: "you shall grant it release, and leave it" (23:11)
note: Land rest is the sabbatical year's core observance, so Ceremonial second. N220 (no sowing) is implied by 'leave it', not stated, so not mixed.

form_basis: "leave it; and the poor … shall eat" (23:11)
note: Produce left for the poor and wild beasts parallels the harvest provisions for the poor: Civil with Moral second.

form_basis: "Do not call to mind … other gods" (23:13)
note: 'Keep everything I have said' is a general exhortation, not a separate requirement, so not mixed.

form_basis: "you shall keep a feast to Me" (23:14)
"Keep the feast of unleavened bread" (23:15)
note: The verse's empty-handed clause is a separate record (C0232), so not mixed.

form_basis: "You shall not appear before Me empty-handed" (23:15)
note: Concerns the gift brought when appearing at the feasts, hence Sacrifice and offerings; the verse's feast-keeping clause is a separate record (C0231).

form_basis: "you shall keep the feast of harvest" (23:16)
"you shall keep … the feast of completion" (23:16)
"you shall not sacrifice … with leaven" (23:18)
"neither shall the fat … remain until morning" (23:18)
"You shall bring the firstfruits" (23:19)
note: Seed N187 belongs to the verse's milk clause, a separate record (C0238), so not mixed.

form_basis: "You shall not boil a lamb" (23:19)
note: The verse's firstfruits clause is a separate record (C0237), so not mixed.

form_basis: "nor do according to their works" (23:24)
note: Also commands destroying their gods: 'you shall utterly overthrow them, and utterly shatter their pillars.'

form_basis: "You shall make no covenant with them" (23:32)
note: A treaty ban in the conquest is Civil; 'nor with their gods' adds an idolatry ban, so Moral second. Moral primary is the alternative.

form_basis: "neither shall they dwell in your land" (23:33)
note: Residence ban in the conquest is Civil; idolatry is its stated motive, not its content, so no Moral second, though Maimonides files N51 under idolatry.

form_basis: "to bring you pure beaten olive oil" (27:20)
"Aaron and his sons shall burn it" (27:21)
"Aaron’s sound shall be heard when he ministers" (28:35)
"Aaron and his sons shall wear them" (28:43)
priestly portion: "shall belong to Aaron and to his sons" (29:28)
succession: "Aaron’s holy robe shall belong to his sons" (29:29)
"An outsider shall not eat them" (29:33)
note: Also requires the priests to eat the consecration offerings: 'They shall eat the things by which they were sanctified.'

form_basis: "it shall not be eaten" (29:34)
note: Also requires burning the remainder: 'you shall burn the remainder with fire.'

form_basis: "shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs" (29:38)
"Aaron shall burn finely ground compounded incense" (30:7)
"You shall not offer other incense" (30:9)
"shall not offer … an offering, or a sacrifice" (30:9)
"you shall not pour a libation on it" (30:9)
"Once a year Aaron shall make expiation" (30:10)
"each shall give the Lord a ransom" (30:12)
note: 'The rich shall give no more and the poor no less' fixes the equal amount within the duty; not a separate prohibition, so not mixed.

form_basis: "shall wash their hands and feet with water" (30:19)
"It shall not be applied to human flesh" (30:32)
"you shall not make anything like it" (30:32)
"You shall not make incense for yourselves" (30:37)
"See that you keep My Sabbaths" (31:13)
note: A restatement of the weekly Sabbath, so Moral with Ceremonial second per the tie-breaker; its framing as Israel's covenant sign could support Ceremonial primary.

form_basis: court penalty: "shall surely be put to death" (31:14)
note: Court penalty: Civil, Moral second (Decalogue Sabbath, Moral per tie-breaker); Ceremonial is the alternative second. Work is barred only through the penalty clauses, so not mixed.

form_basis: "You shall not kindle a fire" (35:3)
note: Seed N322 is the rabbinic court-execution reading of this verse; the plain text forbids kindling fire. A detailed Sabbath rite, so Ceremonial per the tie-breaker.

form_basis: "he shall bring an unblemished male" (1:3)
"his gift shall be fine flour" (2:1)
priestly portion: "what remains … shall be Aaron’s and his sons’" (2:3)
"You shall not make with leaven any sacrifice" (2:11)
"bring neither any leaven nor any honey" (2:11)
note: The firstfruits allowance in 2:12 is a separate record (C0391), so not mixed.

form_basis: "gift of firstfruits you shall bring them" (2:12)
note: Saints Translation says 'you shall bring them', but as an exception to 2:11 it allows leaven and honey as firstfruits, not requiring them. Positive is the alternative reading.

form_basis: "every gift … shall be seasoned with salt" (2:13)
note: Also forbids omitting it: 'You shall not let the salt of the covenant … cease' (N99).

form_basis: "shall bring the sacrifice of the first produce" (2:14)
"he shall bring it unblemished before the Lord" (3:1)
"you shall eat neither any fat" (3:17)
"he shall bring … an unblemished calf" (4:3)
duty to testify: "if he does not declare it" (5:1)
note: Guilt for withholding testimony makes testifying a duty, as P178 counts it; truthful witness is also a moral duty, so Moral second.

form_basis: "he shall confess the sin" (5:5)
note: Confessing sin to God is a lasting duty toward God; here it opens the sliding-scale offering rite (5:6), so Ceremonial second. Ceremonial primary is the alternative.

form_basis: "he shall bring unto the Lord" (5:6)
"He shall pour no oil upon it" (5:11)
note: The flour-bringing clause (5:11a) belongs to the sliding-scale offering with poverty substitutions (C0411); this record is the oil and frankincense ban, so not mixed.

form_basis: priestly portion: "what remains shall be the priest’s" (5:13)
"he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:15)
restitution: "he shall repay … and add a fifth part" (5:16)
note: Restitution is Civil, matching the site label; the property is holy and repaid to the priest beside the guilt offering, so Ceremonial second. Ceremonial primary is arguable.

form_basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:18)
restitution: "he shall return the plunder which he seized" (5:23)
note: Restitution for theft, fraud and false oath: Civil, with Moral second because the underlying acts are moral wrongs.

form_basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:25)
"fire of the altar shall burn upon it" (6:2)
note: Also forbids quenching it: 'and shall not be quenched' (N81).

form_basis: "It shall not be baked with leaven" (6:10)
note: Also requires eating the remainder unleavened in a holy place (6:9), the positive side of the same rule.

form_basis: "and shall not be eaten" (6:16)
note: Also requires burning it wholly. The title leads with burning, but N138 and the contrast with eaten grain offerings make the ban the main clause.

form_basis: "priest who offers it up shall eat it" (6:19)
note: N145 (not outside the court) is implied by 'eaten in a holy place'; the verse states no prohibition, so not mixed.

form_basis: "none of the offerings … shall be eaten" (6:23)
note: Also requires burning them: 'they shall be burned with fire.'

form_basis: "Every male among the priests shall eat them" (7:6)
note: N145 is implied by 'in a holy place'; the verse states no prohibition, so not mixed.

form_basis: priestly portion: "the priest … shall have the hide" (7:8)
priestly portion: "shall belong unto the priest who brings it" (7:9)
priestly portion: "shall belong unto all the sons of Aaron" (7:10)
"shall bring with the sacrifice of praise loaves" (7:12)
"they shall leave none of it until morning" (7:15)
note: Also states the deadline positively ('shall be eaten on the day'). The title leads with eating; the operative limit is the leave-none ban, as N120 counts it.

form_basis: "third day, it shall not be accepted" (7:18)
note: 7:16 sets the two-day window positively; the operative limit is 7:18's third-day ban (N131, N132). Reading 7:16 as a permission is the alternative.

form_basis: "touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten" (7:19)
note: Also requires burning the defiled flesh ('it shall be burned with fire'); 'Whosoever is clean shall eat flesh' allows clean persons to eat.

form_basis: prohibition by penalty: "while his uncleanness is upon him … shall perish" (7:20)
note: Prohibition expressed by the cutting-off penalty ('that soul shall perish'), as N129 counts it.

form_basis: "it shall in no wise be eaten" (7:24)
note: Also permits using such fat for work ('may be used for any work'); a permission, so not mixed.

form_basis: priestly portion: "shall have the right foreleg as his portion" (7:33)
"You shall drink no wine or strong drink" (10:9)
"to distinguish between the holy and the profane" (10:10)
"you shall instruct the sons of Israel" (10:11)
"shall eat the breast … in a holy place" (10:14)
"You shall not eat their flesh" (11:8)
note: 11:2–3 permits animals with both signs ('you may eat'), which Maimonides counts as positive P149; a permission, so not mixed. The operative ban is 11:4, 8.

form_basis: "You shall not … touch their carcasses" (11:8)
note: The verse forbids touching ('shall not … touch'); seed P96 reflects Maimonides counting carcass impurity as a positive status law rather than a ban on touching.

form_basis: "You shall not eat their flesh" (11:11)
note: 11:9 permits finned and scaled creatures ('you may eat'), which Maimonides counts as positive P152; a permission, so not mixed. 'You shall abhor' reinforces the ban.

form_basis: "they shall not be eaten" (11:13)
"winged creeping thing … is an abomination for you" (11:20)
note: Ban by 'abomination' wording; 11:21–22 permits leaping locusts ('you may eat'), which Maimonides counts as positive P151. A permission, so not mixed.

form_basis: status rule: "shall be unclean until evening" (11:24)
status rule: "falls when dead shall become unclean" (11:32)
"it shall not be eaten" (11:41)
note: 'You shall be holy' (11:44) is the motive for the bans, not a separate requirement, so not mixed.

form_basis: status rule: "she shall be unclean seven days" (12:2)
note: 12:4's bans on touching holy things and entering the sanctuary are separate records (C0481, C0482), so not mixed.

form_basis: "She shall touch nothing holy" (12:4)
note: Seed N129 reads 'touch nothing holy' as a ban on eating holy food; the form agrees.

form_basis: "shall not enter the sanctuary" (12:4)
"she shall bring unto the priest" (12:6)
"shall examine him and declare him unclean" (13:3)
